title: Hybrid tiles + railless IA brain dump
content:
Status: rough brain dump, half-sketches, needs wireframe artifacts and a short hallway usability run.

Goal:
- Reduce cognitive load for multi-workspace users (projects, models, routes) while keeping 1-click access to critical flows (run, monitor, rollout).
- Support both rail-first and railless consumption patterns (desktop heavy users vs quick task users).
- Make deep-links and breadcrumbs reliable for support/debugging and for product integrations.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not addressing full permissions matrix here — assume RBAC mapping exists and will be used to prune tiles.
- No changes to backend route names; this doc focuses on surface IA and routing contracts.
- We'll prototype with current token of console CSS variables and a single responsive break-point set.

High-level idea: hybrid tiles + optional rail
- Default visible UI: compact "topic tiles" row at top-left (6–8 tile slots), then a small collapsible rail for pinned actions.
- Tiles represent product areas (Deployments, Jobs, Observability, Models, Eval), each with quick actions (see below).
- Rail is optional: power users can expand to classic left-rail. New users get railless experience (less visual clutter).

Why tiles?
- Faster skim scanning than nested left nav items.
- Works better on narrower screens — tiles wrap to two rows and remain discoverable.
- Encourages surface-level mental model: features as tasks not pages.

Key UX primitives:
- Tile states: normal / active / pinned / alert-badge (counts for issues).
- Escape hatch: floating FAB in top-right of tiles to "Open full nav" (expands left rail).
- Route contract: each tile maps to a route group prefix (e.g., /deployments/*, /models/*) for consistent deep-linking.
- Breadcrumb policy: show up to 3 segments; if >3 show condensed + hover to expand.

Routing & page hierarchy (proposal):
- Root: /console -> redirects to /console/home or last-view depending on user preference.
- /console/home -> tiles overview + quick actions panel
- /console/:area -> area-level shell (Models, Deployments, Observability, Billing, Settings)
  - area index (list): /console/models
  - detail pages: /console/models/:modelId
  - sub-pages: /console/models/:modelId/versions, /console/models/:modelId/evals
- Global query params: ?workspace=xxx & ?view=compact|rail
- Experimental fallback: /console/legacy/* proxies to preexisting routes during rollout.

Progressive disclosure patterns:
- Start tile interaction with a lightweight popover (2–3 quick actions: View list, Create new, Telemetry) to avoid commit to a full page load.
- Popover should be keyboard-navigable and closable via Esc.
- Use incremental loading for area index lists (first 50 items) with a focused search box.

Wireframe notes (desktop -> mobile):
- Desktop default: tiles top-left, search + global actions in topbar, compact rail collapsed to icons.
- Tablet: tiles become 2 rows, rail collapsed; quick actions folded under a chevron.
- Mobile: railless by default; tiles converted to a horizontal swipe list; primary CTA pinned to bottom nav.

Accessibility considerations:
- Tiles are focusable buttons with aria-labels and aria-pressed for pinned state.
- Ensure color contrast for badge counts, and provide text alternatives for icons.
- Announce navigation changes (via live region) when a tile expands into a rail or when route changes from global keyboard navigation.

Telemetry & experimentation plan:
- Metrics to capture: time to first action (from sign-in), tile click-through rate, percent users who expand rail, deep-link success rates, navigation-induced errors.
- A/B tests: Railless default vs Rail default; Tiles with popover quick-actions vs direct page navigation.
- Success criteria: reduce median time to common flows by 25% and increase feature discovery (first-time clicks on Monitoring, Eval) by 20%.

Backlog (initial groom):
- CONS-421: Tiles component + variants (compact / large / with badges) — 3 dev sprints (frontend + unit tests).
- CONS-422: Popover quick-actions — 1 sprint + keyboard/a11y sweep.
- CONS-430: Route contract enforcement + workspace query-parser middleware — 2 sprints.
- CONS-435: Rail expansion animation and persisted preference — 1 sprint.
- CONS-440: Mobile swipe-list implementation + bottom-nav integration — 2 sprints.
- Spike: Performance profiling for tile rendering with 1k workspaces — 3 days.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we keep top-level Billing & Settings as tiles or buried in a profile menu? (tradeoff: discoverability vs noise)
- How aggressive should autohiding be for the rail? If we hide too often power users may feel disoriented.
- Should pinned tiles be user-specific or team-default? (prefer team default with user overrides)

Sketch descriptions for handoff:
- "Tiles grid" (compact): 6 tiles, 3 columns, each tile 140x80, icon + title + small badge count. Hover reveals a 2-line description.
- "Expanded rail" (classic): 64px icon column, 220px expanded width on hover, full labels when pinned.
- "Popover quick-actions": arrow to widest tile edge, list of 3 actions (primary CTA highlighted), small tertiary link to "Open full list".

Support & docs notes:
- Update Console nav principles Confluence page with new routing examples and user preference API.
- Docs: quick start for migrating deep-links (support team to test common customer links).

Next steps (short):
- Convert these notes into two quick candidate mockups (rail-first vs railless-first) and attach to PR. Owner: Marco Diaz. Due: 2024-12-09.
- Run 5 hallway usability sessions with internal SRE/product folks on both prototypes. Owner: Evelyn Chen. Due: 2024-12-16.
- Create a dev spike for deep-link behavior across workspaces. Owner: Jon Park. Due: 2024-12-06.

Notes to self:
- Keep tile text terse. Avoid internal jargon on first touch.
- Consider microcopy for empty states on tiles (ex: "No deployments yet — create one").
- Wire up a small telemetry flag for "tile-hint-shown" to avoid repeating hints forever.

References / inspirations:
- Notion / Figma left rail experiments (small tiles approach)
- Third-party admin consoles that use a tile-first discovery surface

End of brain dump — this is intentionally loose. Will refine into a formal PRD once prototypes and quick metrics are available.
